nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What pressing issue is highlighted in the paragraph regarding global biodiversity?
nodes.answer: The pressing issue highlighted is global biodiversity conservation, particularly in relation to the recent "30 30" target from the Global Biodiversity Framework.
nodes.paragraph: I aim to streamline the publication pro- cess for taxonomists, ensuring their discoveries are shared with the world swiftly and efficiently. We will also actively seek out and promote special issues on relevant topics, including the pressing issue of global biodiversity conservation. The recent "30 30" target from the Global Biodiversity Framework underscores the urgency of this challenge, and we anticipate Kew Bulletin playing a vital role in disseminating research that contributes to its achievement. To nurture and encourage the next generation of taxonomists, we will introduce awards for the best student papers on taxonomy and the best taxonomic treatments published in the journal. These awards will recognise and celebrate outstanding contributions to the field, inspiring future generations of scientists. I am particularly passionate about supporting research that utilises natural history collections, espe- cially herbarium specimens. These collections are invaluable repositories of biodiversity data, yet their significance is often overlooked. I believe it is crucial to emphasise the importance of these collections and encourage researchers to fully leverage the data they contain, especially now that major herbaria worldwide, including Kew, have digitised most of their specimens, making digital images and associated data readily available to the global scientific community for biodi- versity research.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is biodiversity?
nodes.answer: Biodiversity refers to the variety of life on Earth at all levels, from genes to ecosystems, and includes processes that sustain life.

Throughout human history, species have become extinct, and the degradation of ecosystems is likely to accelerate further in the com- ing years (Johnson et al. 2017). Earth S biodiversity is facing an unprecedented crisis, with ecosystems dete- riorating alarmingly due to several sorts of pollution, land-use change (including biodiversity loss, habitat destruction, and fragmentation), climate change, and the introduction of non-indigenous species (NIS) (Gaston et al. 2023). The ocean is no exception, with modified marine ecosystems experiencing accelerat- ing species loss with largely unknown consequences (Boris Worm et al. 2006; Nagelkerken and Connell 2022). In this context, global initiatives, such as the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Frame- work (GBF), have been established to recognise the urgency of these circumstances.

nodes.question: What has contributed to the acceleration of biodiversity loss over the past 50 years?
nodes.answer: The doubling of the human population has contributed to the accelerated loss of biodiversity.

One tool that can help minimize extinction risk, reverse population declines, and bolster biodiversity is the expansion of terrestrial and marine protected areas (Lester et al. 2009; Mace et al. 2018).
